name: Where firms draw their boundaries
idea: A firm keeps an activity inside when running it through the market costs more than running it itself.
suggests: Look at which steps a company builds itself and which it buys, and ask what makes buying costly or risky.
limits: The idea says little about speed, and it can make every in-house choice look like a cost decision.
competing_idea: Capabilities matter as much as costs: a firm may keep a step inside because only it knows how to do it well.
questions: Which steps does the company run itself, and which does it buy?
What would make buying a step riskier than doing it in-house?
Has the company recently moved a step across that line?
